Relations between properties of morphisms

Implications and equivalences for a morphism of schemes, based on Görtz and Wedhorn’s Appendix D.

Appendix DConnected diagramEquivalencesAll relations

The source calls universally injective morphisms purely inseparable. Radicial means universally injective. The labels ft, fp and lfp mean finite type, finite presentation and locally of finite presentation. The labels qc and qcqs mean quasi-compact and quasi-compact quasi-separated, respectively. Dashed arrows require the indicated hypothesis. Heavier arrows are the implications singled out in Appendix D. Select a node or arrow to read its Stacks references. Use Full size to pan the map, or Relations to browse it as text.

Görtz and Wedhorn, Algebraic Geometry I: Schemes, 2nd ed., Appendix D, pp. 585–586

Universal homeomorphism
Definition
Every base change is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces. No isomorphism of structure sheaves is required.
Setting
A universal property holds on the underlying spaces after every scheme base change Y′→YY^{\prime}\to Y.

Flat
Definition

Quasi-projective
Definition
Of finite type and admitting a relatively ample invertible sheaf, in the Stacks convention. Hoyois Definition 4.35(ii) uses a quasi-compact open immersion into a projective scheme over the base. Over a quasi-compact and quasi-separated base the Stacks criterion gives such a factorization.
Setting
Properties of f ⁣:X→Yf\colon X\to Y with conditions on full inverse images, the diagonal, or all base changes.

∞-topos

      Big crystalline site

      Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

      An object is a divided-power thickening U↪TU\hookrightarrow T over (S,ℐ,γ)(S,\mathcal I,\gamma) with an SS-map U→XU\to X. A cover is a Zariski open cover of TT, with UU and its divided-power structure restricted along each open immersion.

                                                            Görtz–Wedhorn, Appendix D

                                                            Valuative (v) topology

                                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                            For a map of qcqs schemes Y→XY\to X, test every Spec⁡V→X\operatorname{Spec}V\to X for a valuation ring VV. There must be an injective local map of valuation rings V↪WV\hookrightarrow W and a lift Spec⁡W→Y\operatorname{Spec}W\to Y over XX. For families, work affine locally on the target and take finite affine refinements whose disjoint union passes the test.

                                                            Grothendieck topologies, sites and topoi

                                                            An object UU is weakly contractible if evaluation at UU sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections.                                                             Appendix D, equivalent descriptions

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a prime pp, a bounded prism (A,I)(A,I) and a smooth pp-adic formal scheme XX over Spf⁡(A/I)\operatorname{Spf}(A/I). Use the bounded absolute site of the same XX.

                                                            Spectrality of the Zariski space

                                                            Equivalence · Qcqs scheme ⇔ Spectral space

                                                            Hypotheses. Let XX be a scheme, and equip ∣X∣|X| with its original Zariski topology.

                                                            Grothendieck diagram

                                                            XX is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if and only if ∣X∣|X| is spectral. Affine opens give a quasi-compact basis, sobriety holds for every scheme, and quasi-separatedness is equivalent to quasi-compactness of affine intersections.

                                                            Equivalent categories

                                                            Equivalence · Spectral space ⇔ Coherent locale

                                                            Also involved · Locale, Spectral map

                                                            Hypotheses. Use classical prime ideal separation, spectral spaces with spectral maps, and coherent locales with maps whose inverse image preserves compact opens.

                                                            Grothendieck diagram

                                                            Taking the locale of opens and taking the space of points give mutually quasi-inverse covariant functors between spectral spaces and coherent locales. Passing to frames of opens instead gives a duality. The compact elements of each frame are the quasi-compact opens of its spectrum.

                                                            Descent of maps into schemes

                                                            descent · Fpqc topology · Classical refinement → Subcanonical topology

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a scheme Z. For each test scheme T, take the presheaf value Hom(T, Z). Use fpqc coverings of schemes.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            Compatible arrows into Z on an fpqc cover descend to a unique arrow T → Z. In particular, the representable presheaves are sheaves.

                                                            Topological invariance of the étale site

                                                            invariance · Universal homeomorphism → Petit étale site

                                                            Hypotheses. Let f : X → Y be a universal homeomorphism of schemes. Use compatible choices for the two small étale sites.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            Base change along f gives an equivalence of the categories of étale schemes over Y and X; it preserves and reflects étale covering families and induces an equivalence of their small étale topoi.

                                                            Affineness over an affine base

                                                            structure morphism · Affine · scheme → Affine · morphism

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S of a scheme over an affine base S.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The scheme X is affine if and only if p is affine. The affine base gives a one-chart test for affineness of the morphism.

                                                            Quasi-compactness over an affine base

                                                            structure morphism · Quasi-compact · scheme → Quasi-compact · morphism

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S over an affine scheme S.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The scheme X is quasi-compact if and only if p is quasi-compact. The inverse image of the single affine chart S is X.

                                                            Stacks 01K4 · affine-open test for a quasi-compact morphism · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                            Quasi-separatedness over an affine base

                                                            structure morphism · Quasi-separated · scheme → Quasi-separated · morphism

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix the structure morphism p : X → S over an affine scheme S.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The morphism p is quasi-separated if and only if intersections of pairs of affine opens of X are quasi-compact, which characterizes quasi-separated X.

                                                            Stacks 01KO · relative affine intersection criterion · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                            Absolute separation via the structure morphism

                                                            structure morphism · Separated · scheme → Separated · morphism

                                                            Hypotheses. For a scheme X use its canonical structure morphism to the spectrum of the integers.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            Separatedness of X means that this specific morphism is separated. The test is whether its relative diagonal is a closed immersion.

                                                            Stacks 01KK · separated morphisms and separated schemes · Hoyois §8.1, opening diagram of local/global and relative/absolute properties

                                                            Quasi-compact opens as a basis

                                                            basis comparison · Qcqs scheme → Qc Zariski basis site

                                                            Hypotheses. Let X be quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Give its quasi-compact opens the induced Zariski coverings.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            Affine opens form a basis. Quasi-compact opens are closed under finite intersection, and coverings of such an open have finite subcovers. Restriction to this basis gives the same sheaves as on all opens.

                                                            Stacks 01KO · quasi-compact intersections · Stacks 009H · comparison of sheaves on a basis

                                                            Open immersion to its open subscheme

                                                            classification · Open immersion → Open subschemes of X

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify two open immersions into X when their sources are isomorphic over X.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            An immersion in this class identifies its source with its open image U equipped with the restriction of the structure sheaf of X. Factorization over X corresponds to inclusion of open subschemes.

                                                            Stacks 01IO · open immersions and open subschemes · Stacks 01HG · the structure sheaf on an open subspace · Hoyois §8.2, classification diagram following Corollary 8.19

                                                            Closed immersion to its closed subscheme

                                                            classification · Closed immersion → Closed subschemes of X, opposite order

                                                            Hypotheses. Fix a target scheme X. Identify closed immersions up to isomorphism of their sources over X. The diagram uses the opposite of the usual inclusion order on closed subschemes.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            A closed immersion i determines a closed subscheme with defining ideal ker(𝒪_X → i_*𝒪_Z). Factorization of one closed immersion through another reverses inclusion of their defining ideals. Passing to the opposite order makes the ideal correspondence order preserving.

                                                            Stacks 01IO · closed immersions and closed subschemes · Stacks 01QO · the quotient-ring description and the quasi-coherent kernel · Hoyois §8.2, classification diagram following Corollary 8.19

                                                            A projective compactification gives a relatively ample line bundle

                                                            Implication · Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense ⇒ Quasi-projective

                                                            Hypotheses. Let X → S factor through a quasi-compact open immersion into a projective S-scheme.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The projective scheme has a relatively ample invertible sheaf. Its restriction to X remains relatively ample, as seen over each affine open of S. The quasi-compact open immersion and the projective morphism are of finite type.

                                                            Marc Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Definition 4.35(ii), the open-in-projective convention · Stacks 07RL · projective implies quasi-projective · Stacks 0B3E · restriction of ampleness along a quasi-compact immersion · Stacks 01VW · finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf · Hoyois, Chapter 8, relative/global panel

                                                            Projective compactification over a qcqs base

                                                            Comparison under hypotheses · Quasi-projective ∧ Qcqs target → Quasi-projective in the open-in-projective sense

                                                            Hypotheses. The target S is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The morphism X → S is of finite type with a relatively ample invertible sheaf.

                                                            Comparison across diagrams

                                                            The morphism factors through an open immersion into a projective S-scheme. This open immersion is quasi-compact because X → S is quasi-compact and the projective S-scheme is separated.

                                                            Stacks 07RM · projective compactification over a qcqs base · Marc Hoyois, Algebraic Geometry, Definition 4.35(ii), the open-in-projective convention · Hoyois, Chapter 8, relative/global panel
